meta.title: Example 1: The Padlocks in Your Mailbox

views.label: 1. Everyone gets their own padlock
views.note: No coordination — Alice puts her padlock on her mailbox, Bob does the same on his. Each keeps the only matching key.

views.label: 2. Bob sends a secret letter
views.note: Bob walks to Alice's mailbox and snaps her padlock shut on the letter — encrypting with her public key.

views.label: 3. Only Alice can open it
views.note: The letter is locked. Bob hasn't got the key, the mailman hasn't either. Alice unlocks with her private key.

cards.title: How the mailbox trick works
items: A padlock = public key — anyone can snap one shut (encrypt to you)
The one key = private key — only its owner opens (decrypt)
The public padlock travels; the private key stays home
Each padlock has its own matching key — locks never "pair up"
